perspective:
Carolyn’s available information / subjective perspective:

- I am Carolyn Abebe, a bank teller. Marilyn Olson is my coworker at the community bank; we recently started working together.
- During a busy, stressful week with increased customer traffic, I noticed Marilyn had been unusually quiet and withdrawn for several days. This seemed unlike her normally engaging demeanor.
- I asked Marilyn if she was alright and whether she wanted to talk. She told me she was overwhelmed with work and some personal stuff, and thanked me for asking.
- In a later interaction, Marilyn responded to me in a curt manner. I felt confused and slightly hurt. I told her I hoped I hadn’t overstepped, that I’d had tough times too, and that talking can sometimes help. She said she appreciated that, apologized if she seemed off, and said it had been a hard week for her.
- After that, Marilyn appeared to respond positively to my openness. I felt relieved and hopeful. I invited her to a small get-together with friends that weekend. She said it sounded lovely, thanked me, and said she’d love to join.
- Despite friendly interactions outside work, I felt Marilyn was still maintaining a professional distance at the bank. I felt disappointed. I asked to talk about our work dynamic, saying I felt a distance I couldn’t quite understand. She said she didn’t realize that, apologized if it seemed that way, and agreed to talk about improving collaboration.
- After our private meeting/talk, I believed we had cleared the air and better understood each other’s professional expectations and personal boundaries. I felt content and optimistic. I proposed teaming up for the new project proposal. Marilyn said it was a great idea, that she was glad we had talked, and that she looked forward to working more closely with me.
- I do not know Marilyn’s private thoughts, hidden reasons, or anything she did not say or show to me.
